name: 21222-prefill-125m-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
architecture: Dense decoder, OPTForCausalLM: 12 layers, hidden 768, 12 heads, head_dim 64, ffn 3072, vocab 50272, max_position_embeddings 2048, float16, ~125M params (~0.25 GB).
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=256, bounded at 30000 requests with a 600 s safety cap, warmup the first 20% and cooldown the last 10% BY REQUEST COUNT (mode: requests, set explicitly on both phases so neither is sized against the safety cap) -- 6000 warmup, 3000 cooldown, 21000 scored. Closed loop rather than a fixed arrival rate: on this card an open-loop rate is either well below the knee, where latency is a flat few milliseconds and insensitive to almost anything, or above it, where latency is arrival backlog -- and where the knee sits moves with the engine, so no single declared rate stays near it. A fixed stream count holds the run in the same regime.
workload: GuideLLM `synthetic_text`, single turn, prompt exactly 700 tokens on the wire (699 once the OPT tokenizer's BOS is counted) and output exactly 2 with ignore_eos, temperature 0.0, request_format `plain` -- this checkpoint's tokenizer has no chat template, so the chat path fails on it. The prompt is assembled as ONE shared 684-token prefix (`prefix_count: 1`, generated once for the whole run) plus a 16-token per-request unique body, rather than 700 freshly generated tokens per request. That is an instrument constraint, not a property of the load: GuideLLM's synthetic generator is single-process and costs 4.68 ms of client CPU per 700-token prompt (measured on this machine with this checkpoint's tokenizer), capping arrivals at ~214/s -- below what this engine retires, so the closed loop could never fill and the card would sit under its own knee whatever the profile asked for. Moving the bulk of the prompt into a once-generated prefix cuts that to 0.59 ms/request (~1700/s) and the loop fills. Prefix caching is off, so the engine cannot exploit the repetition: no block hashing, no reuse, the same 44 KV blocks allocated and released per request, the same 699-token prefill.
purpose: A small 125-million-parameter assistant classifying 700-token documents sharing a long common prefix, 256 concurrent streams, one GPU.
launch:
# Engine args for the pinned commit. Interpreter and hardware: configs/env.yaml (per-machine).
model: facebook/opt-125m
dtype: float16
# Load-bearing, do not restore the default: with prefix caching on, a synthetic corpus lets
# later requests reuse earlier KV and the workload stops being the declared one.
enable-prefix-caching: false
swap-space: 16
disable-log-requests: true
tensor-parallel-size: 1
# Pinned rather than left unset: launched in-process through AsyncLLMEngine the engine resolves
# 128 / 2048 instead, which is not the configuration this item declares.
max-num-seqs: 1024
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
